newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says Italy welcome in EMU if qualifies.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says Italy welcome in EMU if qualifies.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he would be all too happy to see Italy in monetary union providing the nation met the economic criteria set for entry.

Asked by an Italian television reporter if it were true Germany did not want Italy in EMU, Tietmeyer replied, "That is completely untrue. I would be delighted for Italy to join currency union, but it must meet the criteria.

Tietmeyer earlier told reporters it was important for countries trying to get into EMU to achieve a genuine reduction of their deficits and not simply a result which showed a good figure on paper but was the result of accounting tricks.
"Accounting tricks do not resolve problems," he said.
He also rejected the idea of readjusting the EMU timetable.
"I consider a discussion about the timetable wrong," he said.

Countries which want to join EMU have to reach targets on interest and exchange rates, inflation, budgets and public debt. Italy, in common with many other EU countries, is facing problems cutting its deficit to the required level.
